gates.evidence: The proposal targets the memory wall on s03, which is a standard utility feature for the service.
The reward is for playing a mini-game, not for clicking or installing ads.
The proposal uses gain framing ('Unlock 5x Memory') rather than threatening to delete existing content.
The proposal includes an explicit opt-in via a new 'Try for free' button and an invite screen.
The invitation discloses the action (15s game) and the reward (30 mins of memory).
The UI design includes a 'Not Now' button, fulfilling the requirement for free decline.
The offer is placed on the memory paywall screen, not during a chat generation.
The eligibility is explicitly restricted to non-paying users.

scores.evidence: The offer is placed directly on the memory wall (s03), providing exactly what the user needs when they are blocked.
The rewarded play is additive to the free tier without degrading the existing chat experience or quality.
The reward is strictly time-boxed (30m) and capped (2/day), which clearly differentiates it from the 'Janitor Plus' permanent entitlement.
The cost to serve is $0.0090, which exceeds the low-end net revenue per view ($0.0063) computed in code.
Memory context is a core bottleneck for roleplay, making the wall a high-frequency trigger.
Maps to SIM-RWD units using existing screen surfaces.
References Janitor Plus subscription, memory context, and s03 correctly.
Explicit daily cap of 2 and 60-minute cooldown defined.
Includes primary metrics and a user-level holdout experiment plan.

requiredChanges: Resize the reward or switch to a cheaper inference model, as the current cost to serve ($0.0090) exceeds the net revenue per view ($0.0063).
Update economy references to valid items; 'plan' is not a valid economy item in the digest.
parsed.topConcern: The unit economics are currently negative; the cost of providing premium memory context via the rewarded view is higher than the net revenue earned per view.
